response:
Reflection on gen-0 evidence: both surviving signals were weakly powered, and the two binding lessons are (i) every expression must contain a theme-exclusive variable from each side — profitability-exclusive {oibdp, oiadp, ebitda, pi, xsga, xint, xrd} and quality-exclusive {lt, dltt, dlc, act, lct, re} — and (ii) coverage was very low (0.08–0.12), driven by five-year windows and sparse items like xint/oancf. This batch therefore uses widely reported items, short or no windows, and pushes into leverage, liquidity, financing-flow and operating-leverage channels rather than repeating cash-flow validation.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Unlevered Operating Profitability
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Operating profitability that is generated without a large debt stack is durable equity value, whereas the same asset-level profitability at a heavily indebted firm is largely pre-committed to creditors and is more likely to be a levered, cyclical phenomenon.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The profitability leg (EBITDA over assets) and the quality leg (total interest-bearing debt over assets, sign-flipped) are both mapped to bounded ranks, so the product is high only when strong operating margins coincide with a conservative balance sheet, and no firm is forced to an extreme by an unbounded denominator. This directly implements the "durable versus levered profitability" story with two of the best-populated Compustat items, which should keep coverage far above the 0.08 achieved by the xint/oancf construction. It is a level-based leverage channel, distinct from the gen-0 cash-flow-coverage winner.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Profits Not Propped By New Debt
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3)), RANK(NEG(GROWTH(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1))))
HYPOTHESIS: Sustained operating profitability accompanied by shrinking or flat debt reflects genuine internal cash generation, while equally high reported profitability alongside rapid new borrowing signals profits being financed and flattered by balance-sheet expansion that will reverse.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is a flow rather than a level mechanism: it conditions the profitability state on the direction of debt financing over the past year, so it separates self-funding operators from firms whose apparent strength coincides with creditor support. The three-year moving average removes single-year profit noise without imposing the coverage cost of a five-year window. It tests a financing-flow channel that neither gen-0 survivor examined.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Working Capital Backed Profitability
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
HYPOTHESIS: High operating profitability is more likely to persist when the firm holds enough net working capital relative to its total obligations to fund the operating cycle internally, since liquidity-constrained profitable firms must divert operating cash to near-term claims rather than to shareholders.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is the graded repair of the gen-0 binary solvency gate: net working capital scaled by total liabilities enters as a continuous rank, so firms are ordered smoothly by liquidity instead of being dumped en masse into the short leg, which prevents the spread from degenerating into a pure distress bet. Both legs use high-coverage annual items and no time window at all, so it should have the broadest coverage in this batch. It isolates the liquidity channel of financial health, separate from the debt-level channel in Signal 1.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Profitability Validated By Earned Capital
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), RANK(RATIO(re, at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Current operating profitability is credible evidence of a durable franchise when the firm has also accumulated a large stock of retained earnings, because that stock is the audited record of many past profitable years rather than a single good one.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The gen-0 accepted signal paired retained earnings with a five-year profitability TREND and produced a decent Fama-MacBeth slope but essentially zero FF5 alpha; this variant deliberately isolates that design choice by replacing the noisy, coverage-destroying trend with the current profitability level and switching from additive ranks to a multiplicative gate. If alpha improves sharply, the earlier failure was the trend leg and the window length, not the retained-earnings mechanism, which is a directly actionable diagnosis for later generations.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Profitability With Improving Balance Sheet
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(oiadp, at), SUMRANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 1)), DELTA(RATIO(act, lct), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: The market rewards profitability most when financial health is improving at the same time, because deleveraging plus rising liquidity confirms that reported profits are converting into balance-sheet strength rather than being absorbed by working-capital or financing needs.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Unlike the level-based signals above, this Piotroski-style construction uses changes in leverage and in the current ratio as the quality channel, testing whether the direction of financial health, not its level, is the underweighted dimension of profitability durability. Rank aggregation across three channels keeps the score bounded and diversified, which should stabilize portfolio composition and improve the t-statistic on the spread. It gives an informative contrast with Signals 1 and 3, which use the same balance-sheet concepts in levels.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Total Leverage Discounted Profitability
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), RANK(NEG(MUL(RATIO(xsga, sale), RATIO(lt, at)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Profitability is fragile when the firm carries both high fixed operating costs and high financial obligations, because the combined operating-and-financial leverage converts modest revenue shortfalls into large earnings declines; the same profitability at a low-total-leverage firm is far more likely to persist.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The penalty term multiplies an operating-rigidity proxy (SG&A intensity of sales, a profitability-theme item) by a solvency proxy (total liabilities over assets, a quality-theme item), so it captures the compounding of the two leverages rather than either one in isolation. This is a genuinely different mechanism from simple debt-level conditioning: it predicts that fixed-cost-heavy firms need clean balance sheets for their profits to be durable. Both inputs are broadly reported, and the rank product keeps the signal bounded and monotone in each leg.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---CRITIQUE Unlevered Operating Profitability---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: A rank product of high operating profitability and low leverage is essentially the profitability-plus-safety core of the published Quality-Minus-Junk construction, so it rediscovers two well-known standalone anomalies with a trivial multiplicative wrapper rather than testing a new interaction.

---CRITIQUE Profits Not Propped By New Debt---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Conditioning smoothed profitability on the *flow* of debt financing is a coherent and mechanically consistent interaction that goes beyond the level-based leverage gate, though the low-debt-growth leg alone overlaps heavily with the documented debt-issuance/financing anomaly, so the incremental content hinges on the interaction actually paying off.

---CRITIQUE Working Capital Backed Profitability---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The construction is internally consistent and well-scaled, but the stated motivation ("graded repair of the gen-0 binary solvency gate") refers to a signal not present in the archive, and the long leg's preference for high net working capital runs against the documented negative pricing of working-capital/net-operating-asset levels, which should be flagged as a sign risk rather than a fatal flaw.

---CRITIQUE Profitability Validated By Earned Capital---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is a cosmetic variant of the archived "Improving Profits With Earned Capital" signal — same two ingredients with TREND swapped for its own level and SUMRANK swapped for MUL — and both legs (profitability, retained earnings/assets) are individually published anomalies, so it is an ablation dressed up as a new hypothesis.

---CRITIQUE Profitability With Improving Balance Sheet---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The proposal explicitly describes itself as Piotroski-style and combines exactly the F-score's profitability, Δleverage and Δliquidity components, making it a direct rediscovery of a long-published anomaly; the nested SUMRANK also silently double-weights profitability relative to the two change legs.

---CRITIQUE Total Leverage Discounted Profitability---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: The multiplicative operating-times-financial-leverage penalty is a genuinely distinct mechanism from single-dimension leverage conditioning and is monotone and bounded after ranking, but the expected sign puts the signal on a collision course with the documented positive operating-leverage premium (Novy-Marx), which should be treated as the key diagnostic if the slope comes out flat or wrong-signed.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Rollover Risk Adjusted Profitability
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
HYPOTHESIS: What makes profitability fragile is not the amount of debt but its maturity: a profitable firm whose claims are concentrated in debt due within a year must keep refinancing at the mercy of credit markets, so its operating strength is hostage to rollover conditions, while the same profitability financed with long-dated or non-debt claims is insulated.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: The quality leg is the short-term share of the liability structure, which is orthogonal by construction to the leverage level used in Quality-Minus-Junk safety, so this tests maturity composition rather than rediscovering profitability-plus-low-leverage. The interaction is the point: refinancing risk should erode the value of high operating profitability far more than it matters for firms with little profit to protect, and the rank product concentrates the long leg on profitable firms with term-funded balance sheets. Scaling short-term debt by total liabilities rather than assets keeps the measure defined for debt-free firms and avoids simply re-expressing total leverage.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Distribution Verified Profitability
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, DELTA(re, 1)), at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Reported profits are credible when the firm actually hands cash to shareholders; using the retained-earnings identity, income not added to retained earnings is the payout, so profitability accompanied by real distributions reflects durable earning power rather than accounting income that can only ever be reinvested or written off.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This abandons the retained-earnings *stock* channel of the archived signal and instead uses the year-over-year retained-earnings identity to back out implied distributions, a verification mechanism that is economically distinct from a level of accumulated earned capital. The interaction matters because a payout is uninformative at an unprofitable firm and is precisely the hard-cash confirmation that separates durable from paper profitability at a profitable one. Both inputs are widely reported and only a one-year lag is required, so coverage should remain high.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Stable Financing Durable Profits
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(lt, at), 4))))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm with genuinely durable operating strength does not have to keep re-levering and de-levering to fund itself, so an erratic liability-to-assets path reveals funding dependence and earnings fragility even when the current profitability level looks strong.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Replacing the F-score's Δleverage and Δliquidity indicators with the *volatility* of the capital-structure path changes the economic object from a one-year directional improvement to the stability of the financing model, which is not a published score component and cannot be captured by any single-year change. The multiplicative rank form gives each leg equal weight, fixing the silent double-weighting of the nested SUMRANK, and the four-year volatility window is short enough to preserve reasonable coverage. The prediction is a joint one: financing stability should be rewarded mainly where there are substantial profits to sustain.
